reason: Prioritize the classical 32-row packed-A path because it targets the measured n=512 workload and changes the active scratch footprint. The Strassen store change may remove a zeroing pass, but the measured three-buffer Strassen wrapper lost all ten paired runs, so its chance of clearing that regression is uncertain. Vectorizing packing and consolidating allocations target costs in that wrapper, but neither cost is isolated by the measurements; the compiler may already vectorize the loops, and one larger allocation may fail where three smaller ones succeed. The branch rewrite has low correctness risk but no evidence that loop control limits performance. Tail splitting targets general sizes rather than the fixed n=512 timing. Transpose fusion rereads A sixteen times and adds transposes and loop work, giving it the weakest supplied benefit case. All outcomes remain unverified until measured under the fixed gates.
